page: Amazon Web Services m6in.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz and includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

This instance is optimized for network performance, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark results place the server consistently in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1654.0 and a multi-core score of 13933.0. In memory-intensive operations, it registers a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1657.93 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 68.25 GB/sec. Database operations via Redis SET reach 31.22 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is recorded at 35.42 GB/sec.

The lack of local NVMe storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring external EBS volumes for persistent storage. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6in.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for enterprise workloads that require high network throughput without the premium cost of dedicated memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Performance on large language models is a notable limitation, with the 70B model prompt processing benchmark scoring in the weak tier at 6.22 tokens per second. Consequently, this instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale text or image processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and a 3.5 GHz clock speed. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most tasks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 13933.0 and a static web serving throughput of 35.42 GB/sec. While it demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models, it exhibits weak performance on larger 70B models. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for network-heavy, general-purpose workloads such as database operations, software compilation, and web serving, where local storage is not a primary requirement.
